newsitem.title: JAPAN: Sakakibara sees little effect from forex reforms.
newsitem.headline: Sakakibara sees little effect from forex reforms.

text.p: Eisuke Sakakibara, director-general of the Ministry of Finance's (MOF) International Finance Bureau, said on Wednesday he was not worried about a "hollowing out" of Japan's financial sector as a result of planned foreign exchange reforms.

Sakakibara was asked by an opposition parliament member if he was worried about foreign exchange reforms taking place ahead of planned financial sector and tax deregulation as that could cause a hollowing out of Japan's financial industry.
Sakakibara said implementing sweeping deregulation was important. He explained that even the United States and Britain first implemented foreign exchange deregulation before financial sector reforms.
If there is going to be a big time lag between the implementation of foreign exchange deregulation and deregulation of the financial industry, there could be a hollowing out, he said.
But if financial deregulation is carried out soon after the foreign exchange reforms in April next year, "I don't think we need to worry about a 'hollowing out'," Sakakibara said.

Sakakibara also said that he does not expect Japanese companies to substantially increase the use of foreign currencies when settling their business transactions after the foreign exchange reforms are implemented.
Although it is theoretically possible for Japanese companies to settle accounts in foreign currencies, Sakakibara said he did not think that would become a trend.

A senior official from MOF's tax bureau told the same parliamentary session that the ministry was already discussing with financial institutions on what tax revisions needed to be made in line with the foreign exchange law reforms.
The official said that the ministry would like to prepare the tax revisions as quickly as possible, including submitting them to an extraordinary session of parliament if one is held later this year.
